title: Technical Drawing: Orthographic, Isometric and Perspective
summary: First-angle orthographic projection with hidden detail, converting between orthographic and isometric views, one- and two-point perspective, dimensioning rules and working drawings.

notes.text: A **working drawing** gives all the information needed to make a product: accurate views, **dimensions**, materials, scale and a title block. It is usually drawn in **first-angle orthographic projection**.

rows: To the **right** of the front view

notes.label: Remember
notes.text: First-angle projection is shown by its symbol: a truncated cone drawn with a front view and a side view. Hidden edges are drawn as thin **dashed** lines, and holes have **centre lines** (long dash, short dash).

notes.title: Where does each view go?
notes.problem: In first-angle projection, where do you draw the top view and the view from the left, relative to the front view?
steps: Imagine rolling the object: the view you see goes on the far side of the object.
The top view goes below the front view.
The left view goes to the right of the front view.
notes.answer: Top view below; left view on the right.

items: Draw an isometric **crate** (box) using the overall length, width and height from the orthographic views: verticals stay vertical; length and width lines are at 30°.
Mark the positions of features on the edges of the crate, measuring only along the three isometric axes.
Join the points and erase construction lines. Darken the outlines.
Circles become ellipses in isometric drawing.

notes.label: Common mistake
notes.text: In isometric drawing you may only measure true lengths **along** the isometric axes. Sloping (inclined) lines must be found by marking their end points first and then joining them.

rows: One vanishing point on the horizon line; front faces are drawn flat and all depth lines go towards the vanishing point
Drawing a road, a room or a passage seen from the front
Two vanishing points on the horizon line; vertical lines stay vertical and all other edges go to one of the two points
Drawing buildings and products seen from a corner

notes.caption: One-point perspective. All depth lines run to one vanishing point on the horizon line.

notes.text: The **horizon line** is at the viewer's eye level. Objects drawn above it are seen from below; objects below it are seen from above. Perspective makes objects look realistic because distant parts appear smaller, but measurements cannot be taken from it.

items: Dimensions are in **millimetres**; the unit is not written.
Dimension lines are thin, with arrowheads touching the **extension (projection) lines**; leave a small gap between the object and the extension line.
Numbers are written above the dimension line, readable from the **bottom** or the **right-hand side** of the page.
Do not dimension the same feature twice; place dimensions outside the view where possible.
Circles are dimensioned with Ø (diameter) and arcs with R (radius).

notes.title: Find the mistakes
notes.problem: A drawing has a dimension written as '50 mm', a vertical dimension that reads from the left, and dimension lines crossing each other. What should change?
steps: Dimensions are in millimetres, and the unit is left out of each number and stated in the title block: write 50.
Vertical dimensions must read from the right-hand side of the page.
Dimension lines should not cross, so place the shorter ones nearest the object.
notes.answer: Remove the unit, rotate the text to read from the right, and rearrange the lines.

notes.text: A title block in the bottom right corner shows the **title** of the drawing, the **name** of the person who drew it, the **date**, the **scale**, the **projection symbol** and the **drawing number**.

questions.prompt: In first-angle projection, where is the left view placed?
options: To the left of the front view
To the right of the front view

questions.prompt: What type of line shows hidden edges? (one word: … lines)
In isometric drawing, a circle is drawn as…
How many vanishing points are used in two-point perspective?
Which symbol is placed before a diameter dimension?
Accurate measurements can be taken from a perspective drawing.
Match each view to its position in first-angle projection.
Give THREE rules for dimensioning a working drawing.
questions.memo: Any three (1 each): dimensions in mm without unit; thin dimension lines with arrowheads; numbers readable from bottom or right; no duplicate dimensions; place outside the view; Ø for diameter and R for radius; small gap between object and extension lines

questions.prompt: Name THREE items that must appear in a title block.
questions.memo: Any three (1 each): title; name; date; scale; projection symbol; drawing number

questions.prompt: Why would a designer use two-point perspective to present a product to a client?
questions.memo:
✓ It makes the product look realistic / as the eye sees it (1)
✓ so the client can easily imagine what it will look like (1)
